anchors.text: A source states a full kettle boils in under 150 seconds.
A source states a full kettle boils in 150 to 210 seconds.
A source states a full kettle takes more than 210 seconds to boil.

definition.objective: The morning queue at the kettle is short because a full kettle boils quickly
definition.question: How long does this kettle take to boil a full kettle of water, as the maker states it?
definition.evidenceRule: The maker's manual or specification page stating a boil time for a full kettle, with the volume stated; a retailer's or reviewer's measured time counts as secondary; a general claim such as 'rapid boil' does not count, and neither does a time for a part-filled kettle.

missingRules.when: No source gives a boil time for a full kettle.
Sources give different boil times for a full kettle, or give a time without saying what volume or starting temperature it is for.

exclusions: Keep-warm, re-heat or partial-fill boil times.
Electricity used per boil; that is not this criterion.

reply:
Added as a new criterion; it does not overlap or change any of the three existing ones (repair-policy, spare-parts, quietness), so there are no overlap probes. criteria_set came back with revised empty, no superseded cells and no definitionGaps. I did not score or blank any cell, and I left the existing criteria exactly as they were.

Here is the criterion for you to confirm:
- Boil time (boil-time), direction: decreasing, because you said faster is better.
- Objective: the morning queue at the kettle is short because a full kettle boils quickly.
- Question a scorer answers: how long does this kettle take to boil a full kettle of water, as the maker states it?
- Anchors (levels follow the time, so level 1 is fastest): 1 = a source states a full kettle boils in under 150 seconds; 3 = a source states 150 to 210 seconds; 5 = a source states more than 210 seconds.
- Evidence rule: the maker's manual or spec page stating a full-kettle boil time with the volume; a retailer's or reviewer's measured time is secondary; "rapid boil" and part-filled times do not count.
- Missing rules: not-evidenced when no source gives a full-kettle boil time; indeterminate when sources disagree or give a time without the volume or starting temperature.
- Exclusions: boiling noise (that is quietness); keep-warm, re-heat or part-fill times; electricity used per boil.

The 150 and 210 second thresholds are my guess, since kettle capacities differ and you gave no numbers. Please confirm or change them, and tell me whether "full" should mean each kettle's own maximum fill or one fixed volume for all three. Nothing in the new column is scored until you confirm.

Which of those do you mean, and why does it matter for this decision? A sentence in your own words about what would make one kettle count as more sustainable than another is enough, and I will turn it into a defined column. Nothing has been written to the analysis.

I have not added a column, because this is already covered: spare-parts asks "For how long does the maker state it stocks spare parts?", scored from a maker's statement of how many years parts are stocked (level 1 none sold, 3 under five years, 5 ten years or more). Overlaps: spare-parts.

Here is the question that decides it: take two kettles identical on everything except how many years the maker keeps parts in stock; do you prefer one, or are you indifferent? If you prefer the longer-stocked one, that is what spare-parts already measures and no new column is needed. If you mean something spare-parts does not capture (for example a finer year scale than the 1/3/5 anchors, which would be a revision of spare-parts and mean re-scoring any cell already recorded under it), tell me the reason and I will take it from there.
